questions.stem: The main difference between pictorial painting and decorative painting is that pictorial painting
options: is always done on walls, while decorative painting is on canvas
represents a subject or idea as a picture, while decorative painting mainly beautifies surfaces and objects
is never sold, while decorative painting is sold
questions.explanation: Pictorial painting communicates a scene, story or idea; decorative painting adorns walls, bodies, furniture and objects.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ELEMENT of design?
questions.explanation: Elements are the building blocks (line, shape, colour, texture, form, space); balance, rhythm and emphasis are principles.

questions.stem: The principle of design that makes one part of a painting attract attention first is
questions.explanation: Emphasis creates a focal point through contrast of colour, size or placement.

questions.stem: In a painting, repeating similar shapes and colours at regular intervals to lead the eye across the picture creates
questions.explanation: Rhythm is visual movement created by repetition; contrast places opposites side by side.

questions.stem: In the traditional painter's colour wheel, the three primary colours are
questions.explanation: Pigment primaries (RYB) cannot be mixed from other colours; red, green, blue are light primaries.

questions.stem: Mixing equal amounts of blue and yellow paint produces
questions.explanation: Blue + yellow gives the secondary colour green.

questions.stem: Which pair of colours are complementary?
questions.explanation: Complementary colours lie opposite each other on the colour wheel: red-green, blue-orange, yellow-violet.

questions.stem: A colour obtained by adding white to a hue is called a
questions.explanation: Adding white gives a tint; adding black gives a shade.

questions.stem: A colour scheme using yellow, yellow-green and green, which lie next to one another on the colour wheel, is
questions.explanation: Analogous colours are neighbours on the wheel and give harmony.

questions.stem: Yellow-orange is classified as a
questions.explanation: Tertiary colours are made by mixing a primary with a neighbouring secondary, e.g. yellow + orange.

questions.stem: Camwood and kaolin are local sources that a Nigerian painter can use to improvise
questions.explanation: Camwood (osun) gives red; kaolin (white clay) gives white.

questions.stem: Applying paint so thickly that brush or knife marks stand out from the surface is called
questions.explanation: Impasto gives a raised, textured surface; glazing uses thin transparent layers.

questions.stem: Painting with pigments mixed with egg yolk as the binder is known as
questions.explanation: Egg tempera uses egg yolk; encaustic uses hot wax and fresco uses wet lime plaster.

questions.stem: In true (buon) fresco, the pigments are applied on
options: wet lime plaster so they become part of the wall as it dries
questions.explanation: The pigments bind chemically with the setting lime plaster, making a very durable mural.

questions.stem: Laying a thin transparent layer of colour over a completely dry underpainting to modify its colour is
questions.explanation: Glazes let light pass through to the layer below, giving depth and luminosity.

questions.stem: Applying fresh colours onto areas that are still wet so they blend softly is
questions.explanation: Wet-in-wet lets colours merge; dry brush gives broken, scratchy strokes.

questions.stem: A picture or design made by fixing small pieces of coloured glass, stone or tile together on a surface is a
questions.explanation: Mosaic uses small pieces called tesserae; a mural is painted directly on a wall.

questions.stem: A large painting executed directly on a wall or ceiling is a
questions.explanation: Murals are wall paintings; easel paintings are portable works on canvas or board.

questions.stem: Rolling a crumpled cloth over a wet glaze coat to produce a textured, broken pattern is
questions.explanation: Rag rolling lifts or applies glaze with a rag to give a soft broken texture.

questions.stem: Dragging a toothed tool through a wet glaze to create lines and wavy patterns on a wall is
questions.explanation: Combing produces parallel or wavy lines by removing glaze with teeth of a comb.

questions.stem: The decorative technique that gives an evenly coloured, smooth finish with no texture or pattern is
questions.explanation: Flat painting applies uniform colour; scumbling and rag rolling deliberately break the colour.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: A painting of an arrangement of fruits, pots and cloth on a table is a
questions.explanation: Still life represents inanimate objects arranged by the artist.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: A painting composed from the artist's memory and fantasy rather than from direct observation is
questions.explanation: Imaginative compositions come from the mind; observational work is done from what is seen.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: Painting from a live human model posed in the studio is known as
questions.explanation: Life painting studies the human figure directly from a model.

questions.topic: Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting
questions.stem: Which of the following is a social FUNCTION of pictorial painting?
options: Recording historical events and cultural practices
questions.explanation: Pictorial paintings document events and culture, educate and communicate; protection of surfaces is a function of paint coatings.

questions.stem: Uli is a traditional body and wall painting art associated mainly with the
questions.explanation: Uli designs drawn with dark plant dye are an Igbo tradition, practised especially by women.

questions.stem: The reddish-brown plant dye widely used by Hausa and Fulani women to decorate hands and feet is
questions.explanation: Henna leaves are ground into a paste that stains the skin reddish-brown.

questions.stem: A major difference between traditional and modern body decoration is that modern body decoration
options: often uses manufactured cosmetics and tattoo inks rather than local plant and mineral dyes
questions.explanation: Traditional body art used local materials (uli, henna, camwood, kaolin); modern practice mostly uses factory-made products.

questions.stem: Which material is used to decorate interior walls by pasting printed patterned paper?
questions.explanation: Wallpaper is printed paper fixed with adhesive; terrazzo is a floor finish.

questions.stem: The traditional relief and painted decorations on the facades of houses in old Zaria and Kano are associated with the
questions.explanation: Hausa builders decorate mud facades with raised and painted motifs (zanen gida).

questions.stem: One function of wall decoration in a public building is to
options: create a pleasant environment and express the identity of the users
reduce the weight of the roof
questions.explanation: Decoration improves appearance and communicates culture or corporate identity.

questions.stem: In linear perspective, parallel lines receding from the viewer appear to meet at the
questions.explanation: Receding parallels converge at a vanishing point on the eye level (horizon line).

questions.stem: Making distant hills paler, bluer and less detailed than nearer ones is an example of
questions.explanation: Atmospheric perspective imitates the effect of air and haze on distant objects.

questions.stem: A drawing of a building viewed from one corner, with two sets of horizontal edges receding to two points on the horizon, uses
questions.explanation: When the corner faces the viewer, both sets of horizontal edges recede to separate vanishing points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a career directly related to decorative painting?
questions.explanation: Interior decorators plan colour schemes and finishes for interiors.

questions.stem: One socio-economic value of painting to a community is that it
options: creates jobs and income through commissions, sales and tourism
questions.explanation: Painting provides employment, earns income and attracts tourism while preserving culture.

questions.stem: An artist charges ₦9,000 per square metre for labour on a mural 6 m long and 3 m high, plus ₦45,000 for materials. The total charge is
Which factor should NOT normally affect the price an artist charges for a decorative wall painting?
options: Time required to complete the work
questions.explanation: Pricing depends on size, location, materials, time and quality, not on personal tastes unrelated to the work.

questions.stem: A printed booklet listing the titles, sizes, media and prices of works on show at an exhibition is the
questions.explanation: Catalogues inform visitors and buyers about each exhibited work.

questions.stem: When a gallery sells a painting on behalf of an artist and keeps an agreed percentage of the price, the percentage is called
questions.explanation: Galleries and agents earn a commission on sales; the artist receives the balance.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of colour. [2 marks]
(b) Classify colours into primary, secondary and tertiary, giving examples of each. [6 marks]
(c) Describe the following colour schemes: (i) analogous (ii) complementary (iii) monochromatic. [6 marks]
(d) Name one local source of colour. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Colour is the visual sensation produced when light of different wavelengths is reflected from a surface into the eye (hue)
2 marks: (b) Primary: colours that cannot be produced by mixing others - red, yellow, blue
2 marks: (b) Secondary: made by mixing two primaries - orange, green, violet
2 marks: (b) Tertiary: made by mixing a primary with an adjacent secondary - e.g. red-orange, yellow-green, blue-violet
2 marks: (c)(i) Analogous: colours next to one another on the colour wheel, e.g. yellow, yellow-green, green
2 marks: (c)(ii) Complementary: colours opposite on the colour wheel, e.g. red and green, blue and orange
2 marks: (c)(iii) Monochromatic: tints, tones and shades of a single hue
1 mark: (d) Any one: camwood (red); kaolin/chalk (white); charcoal/soot (black); indigo (blue); laterite (red-brown); henna; uli
questions.explanation: Colour is the sensation of reflected light. Primaries red, yellow, blue; secondaries orange, green, violet; tertiaries such as red-orange. Analogous colours are neighbours; complementary are opposites; monochromatic uses one hue in tints and shades. Local sources: camwood, kaolin, charcoal, indigo.

questions.stem: Describe each of the following techniques in pictorial painting, stating one material or tool used: (a) impasto (b) glazing (c) fresco (d) tempera (e) dry brush painting. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Impasto: paint applied very thickly so that brush/knife marks stand up from the surface, giving texture (2); tool - palette knife or stiff brush, oil/acrylic paint (1)
3 marks: (b) Glazing: thin transparent layer of colour over a dry layer to modify colour and give depth (2); material - glazing medium/oil or acrylic diluted with medium (1)
3 marks: (c) Fresco: painting with water-based pigments on freshly laid wet lime plaster so the colour becomes part of the wall (2); material - lime plaster, pigments (1)
3 marks: (d) Tempera: pigment bound with egg yolk (or glue), dries quickly to a matt finish, applied in thin layers (2); material - egg yolk, pigment, gesso panel (1)
3 marks: (e) Dry brush: a brush with little paint dragged lightly over the surface so colour catches only on raised texture, giving broken strokes (2); tool - stiff bristle brush (1)
questions.explanation: Impasto: thick textured paint with knife or stiff brush. Glazing: thin transparent layer over dry paint. Fresco: pigments on wet lime plaster. Tempera: pigment in egg yolk. Dry brush: little paint dragged lightly for broken effects.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of body decoration. [2 marks]
(b) State three differences between traditional and modern body decoration. [6 marks]
(c) Name four materials used for traditional body decoration in Nigeria. [4 marks]
(d) State three functions of body decoration. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The art of beautifying the human body with designs using paints, dyes, marks or ornaments for aesthetic, social or ritual purposes
6 marks: (b) Any three, 2 marks each: traditional uses local dyes (uli, henna, camwood, kaolin) while modern uses manufactured cosmetics/tattoo inks; traditional motifs carry cultural meanings while modern designs are often fashion-driven; traditional linked to ceremonies/rites while modern for everyday fashion; traditional often temporary natural stains while modern can be permanent tattoos
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: uli; henna (lalle); camwood (osun); kaolin/white clay (efun); charcoal; antimony/kohl (tiro/kwalli); indigo
3 marks: (d) Any three, 1 mark each: beautification; identification of ethnic group or status; ceremonial/ritual purposes (marriage, festivals, initiation); protection/healing beliefs; communication of social messages
questions.explanation: Body decoration beautifies the body with designs. Traditional practice uses local dyes and meaningful motifs for ceremonies; modern practice uses factory cosmetics and fashion designs. Materials: uli, henna, camwood, kaolin, charcoal, kohl. Functions: beauty, identity, ritual, status, communication.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of perspective in painting. [2 marks]
(b) Describe the following: (i) one-point perspective (ii) two-point perspective (iii) aerial perspective. [9 marks]
(c) State four ways an artist shows depth in a landscape painting. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The method of representing three-dimensional objects and space on a flat surface so that they appear to recede into the distance as seen by the eye
3 marks: (b)(i) One-point: lines receding from the viewer converge to a single vanishing point on the horizon/eye level; used when viewing a road or room straight on
3 marks: (b)(ii) Two-point: object viewed from a corner; horizontal edges recede to two vanishing points on the horizon, verticals stay vertical
3 marks: (b)(iii) Aerial/atmospheric: distant objects shown paler, bluer, less detailed and with less contrast than near objects
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: overlapping objects; diminishing size with distance; placing distant objects higher on the picture plane; lighter, cooler colours in the distance; less detail and texture in the distance; converging lines
questions.explanation: Perspective represents depth on a flat surface. One-point: lines converge to one vanishing point; two-point: a corner view with two vanishing points; aerial: distance shown by paler, bluer, softer forms. Depth cues: overlap, diminishing size, position, cooler colours, less detail, converging lines.

questions.stem:
An artist in Abeokuta is commissioned to produce three framed paintings. Materials: canvases ₦12,000 each, paints ₦28,000, brushes and other sundries ₦6,500, frames ₦15,000 each. She works 40 hours at ₦2,500 per hour.
(a) Calculate (i) the total cost of materials (ii) the labour cost (iii) the total cost of the job. [8 marks]
(b) If she adds 25% profit on total cost, calculate the price to be charged. [3 marks]
(c) State four factors, apart from cost, that may affect the price of a painting. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Materials = 36,000 + 28,000 + 6,500 + 45,000 = ₦115,500
2 marks: (a)(ii) Labour = 40 x 2,500 = ₦100,000
3 marks: (a)(iii) Total cost = ₦115,500 + ₦100,000 = ₦215,500
3 marks: (b) Price = ₦215,500 x 1.25 = ₦269,375
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: reputation of the artist; size of the work; quality/originality; demand and market location; deadline/urgency; client's budget/negotiation; medium used
questions.explanation: Materials ₦115,500; labour ₦100,000; total cost ₦215,500; with 25% profit the price is ₦269,375. Other factors: reputation, size, quality, demand, location, urgency, negotiation.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe five steps in planning an art exhibition. [10 marks]
(b) State three ways of funding an exhibition. [3 marks]
(c) State two outlets for selling paintings. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: decide theme, type (solo/group) and dates; select and prepare/frame the works; book a suitable venue/gallery; prepare a budget and seek funds; publicise (invitations, posters, social media, press); prepare catalogue and labels with prices; mount/hang the works and arrange lighting; opening ceremony, sales record and security; dismantle and evaluate
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: personal savings; sponsorship by companies; grants from arts councils/government/NGOs; gate fees; sale of catalogues; donations/patrons; loans
2 marks: (c) Any two, 1 mark each: art galleries; online platforms/social media; art fairs and festivals; hotels and corporate offices; direct commissions; auctions
questions.explanation: Plan the theme and dates, select and frame works, book a venue, budget and raise funds, publicise, prepare a catalogue, hang and light the works, host the opening, then evaluate. Funding: savings, sponsors, grants, fees, donations. Outlets: galleries, online, fairs, hotels, commissions, auctions.
